Union Cabinet has approved the development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the North and South Block complex in New Delhi. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation.

The Cabinet has also approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for RABI Season, 2026-27 on Phosphatic and Potassic fertilizers. The tentative budgetary requirement for Rabi 2026-27 will be approximately 62 thousand 370 crore rupees. This is nearly 24 thousand 417 crore more than the budgetary requirement for Rabi 2025-26 season. Mr Vaishnaw said the subsidy will ensure smooth availability of these fertilizers to the farmers at affordable prices.

The Cabinet has also given nod to the continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031.

The Cabinet has also cleared the extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of Noida Metro Rail Project covering approximately 8.5 kilometres and comprising five elevated stations.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stated that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will transform New Delhi into a global centre of cultural heritage, with the world’s largest museum display area. In a social media post, the Prime Minister noted that the Cabinet’s decision will give impetus to the transformation of the historic North and South Block buildings into a magnificent celebration of India’s civilisational journey.

Mr Modi said the museum will showcase thousands of years of India’s heritage through world-class galleries and immersive experiences. It will cover a wide range of subjects, including ancient knowledge systems, mathematics, astronomy, architecture, art, languages, and spirituality. He highlighted that these buildings, which have long served as centres of governance, will now become places where millions can discover, experience, and celebrate the timeless richness of India’s civilisation.

The Prime Minister described the initiative as a historic new chapter in India’s cultural heritage.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi this evening. Around 2,000 farmers from across India, alongside policymakers, diplomats, industry leaders, and agricultural scientists are attending the 2-day event. Approximately 20 progressive farmers and Padma Shri recipients are scheduled to share their innovation and resilience stories. Discussions center on increasing farmer incomes, adopting precision farming and artificial intelligence-led resource management, developing climate-resilient crops, and expanding India’s agricultural exports.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two day visit to Karnataka and Gujarat beginning tomorrow.

Mr Modi will participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram,  the residential headquarters campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA) tomorrow morning. In the afternoon, the Prime Minister will flag off and undertake a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station. After this, Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 15 thousand 600 crore rupees in Bengaluru.

On the same day, the Prime Minister will travel to Mysuru where, he will participate in a tree plantation programme at Bharat Vann. In the evening, he will inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium.

Government has rationalized the visa regime by reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to 9 and the number of sub-categories from 49 to 23. Ministry of Home Affairs said that the move is aimed at boosting foreign tourist arrivals, enhance medical value travel and foreign student arrivals. The step follows the earlier rationalisation undertaken in October last year when the main visa categories were reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49. Ministry said that the required filed and column for all 23 categories and sub-categories of Visas have been reduced by 65 to 70 per cent.

Today is the Public Service Broadcasting Day. The day is observed every year on this day to mark the historic address of Father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi, through Akashvani. An important day in the History of Broadcasting, Mahatma Gandhi paid his first and only visit to the Broadcasting House in New Delhi on this day in 1947. More from our correspondent:

“On this day in 1947, Mahatma Gandhi addressed the grief-stricken people staying in Kurukshetra who were displaced during partition through a special broadcast. In the year 2000, then Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting, Sushma Swaraj announced that every 12th of November would henceforth be observed as Public Service Broadcasting Day. Since then, Akashvani has been celebrating the occasion every year with special programmes and events. Akashvani music artists render bhajans dear to Mahatma Gandhi to mark these celebrations. Throughout the year, Akashvani broadcasts and organizes a series of special programmes across the country based on the Gandhian Philosophy. Public Service Broadcasting Day inspires Broadcasters to carry forward the ideals and teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, to every corner of the country. With Arzoo, Samarth Singh for Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The Northern Railway is operating 29 Special trains from major railway stations in the Delhi region today. The move is aimed at facilitating passengers travelling to their native places to celebrate the Chhath festival. The move is part of the elaborate arrangements made by Northern Railway at major stations of Delhi Area for the convenience of passengers, especially those travelling to the Eastern parts of the country to celebrate the festival of Chhath.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs will organise a two-day National Tribal Literary Festival beginning today at India Habitat Centre in New Delhi. The Literary Festival is being held as part of the celebrations commemorating Janjatiya Gaurav Divas 2026. The festival aims to provide a national platform for celebrating India’s rich and diverse tribal literary traditions, promoting indigenous languages and oral narratives, and recognising the contributions of tribal writers, poets, storytellers and knowledge holders. The inaugural session will be attended by Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram.

Iran has refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or resume negotiations with the United States until Washington meets seven conditions set by Tehran. We have a report:

“Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that Tehran has sent its demands to Washington but is awaiting an official response. He warned President Donald Trump against renewed military action, saying it will result in another US defeat. Senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei also said no negotiations are underway and warned that Iran can target US military bases outside the Middle East if they were used to launch attacks against the country. Iran’s demands include lifting US sanctions, releasing frozen assets, ending the naval blockade of Iranian ports, compensation for war damage and an end to fighting across regional fronts, including Lebanon. Tehran’s proposal calls for reopening the Strait of Hormuz six days after Washington meets its demands, with negotiations on a final agreement beginning the following day. Jigyasa Pandey, Akashvani News Delhi.”

Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Keralam, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for the day. IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea till the 16th of this month.

An earthquake measuring 4.9 on the Richter scale shook Darjeeling and adjoining areas of North Bengal in the early hours today. The tremors were recorded at around 4:30 AM. According to the National Centre for Seismology, the earthquake had its epicentre in Nepal. Tremors were felt across several parts of North Bengal and neighbouring regions. Residents, particularly those living in high-rise buildings, were startled by the sudden shaking, with many rushing outdoors as a precaution.

Indian boxers, Gunjan and Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei have stormed into the finals of the Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, keeping India’s hopes of two gold medals alive. Gunjan beat Great Britain’s Lily Bassett 4-1 in the women’s 48-kilogram semifinal yesterday. She will now face Algeria’s Bouthaina Bensalah in the final. Meetei was actually the first Indian boxer to reach the finals at these Youth Olympics. He got to the men’s 50-kilogram final after winning 5-0 against Izzon Jeffrey Galea Arevalo from Colombia in the semifinal bout. Meetei will face Kristian Jubani from Ireland for the gold.

So far, India have won nine medals at the Games, including three silver and six bronze in wrestling, boxing, and swimming. This Youth Olympics 2026 ends on the 13th of this month.

President Droupadi Murmu will confer Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 at a ceremony in New Delhi today. These awards honour India’s cleanest cities, celebrating their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban. Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal, and Minister of State of the Ministry Tokhan Sahu will be present on the occasion.

 

“The Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 awards serve as a celebration of the collective achievements of cities and States and a renewed commitment to sustain on-ground achievements. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs informed that the 10th edition of the Swachh Survekshan on the theme of ‘Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel- Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath’ has been successfully completed. It said that Swachh Survekshan has grown from 73 Urban Local Bodies in 2016 to more than four thousand cities in its latest edition. Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 introduced several key enhancements, including greater emphasis on citizen feedback, expanded coverage of Urban River Fronts, and focused indicators on prevention of open defection and open urination and behaviour change initiatives in schools. As part of the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan, Urban Local Bodies were evaluated across 43 indicators spanning 10 key assessment areas. SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHVANI NEWS , DELHI.”

Government has invited fresh applications under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices (PLI-MD), which has now been extended up to the year 2035-36. An outlay of approximately two thousand 700 crore rupees available under the scheme will be utilized for the purpose. The applicants can submit applications through an online portal, which will be operational in the next 10 days. The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers said that on the basis of learnings in the first phase of the Scheme, a number of simplifications have been done in the eligibility conditions as well as procedure for claiming incentive by the applicants.

 

The applicants shall be allowed three years for setting up their manufacturing facilities in any of the four Target Segments (TS) which are medical consumables, disposables and implants, Critical components, high-end medical devices which are presently at a nascent stage of domestic manufacturing and high-end medical devices that are presently only assembled in the country.

In view of the Chhath festival, Northern Railway has planned to run 31 special trains from major stations in the Delhi area from today. Northern Railway has made elaborate arrangements at major railway stations in the Delhi area to manage the rush of passengers travelling to their native places to celebrate the Chhath festival, particularly those heading towards eastern parts of the country.

 

27 special trains wre operated from major stations in the Delhi region yesterday. These include nine trains from Anand Vihar Terminal, six from New Delhi, five from Shakur Basti, three each from Delhi Junction and Hazrat Nizamuddin, and one from Rohtak.

Delhi government has declared public holiday on November 16 on the occasion of Chhath Puja. Schools, colleges, government offices and premises of autonomous bodies under Delhi government will remain closed on that day. The offices of the civic agencies, including the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and New Delhi Municipal Council will also observe the Chhath holiday.

The portals of Kedarnath and Yamunotri shrines in Uttarakhand will be closed for the winter season today on the auspicious occasion of Bhai Dooj. This year, Kedarnath witnessed over 19 lakh pilgrims, while nearly eight lakh fifty thousand devotees visited Yamunotri Dham.

 

“In Rudraprag district, the portals of Kedarnath Dham, will be closed at 8:30 AM today. Following the closure, the ceremonial Utsav Doli of Baba Kedar will proceed to the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, the winter seat of the deity, where devotees can seek blessings during the winter months. District Magistrate Vishal Mishra said that all arrangements for the closure of the temple have been completed.

 

Meanwhile, the portals of Yamunotri Dham, located in Uttarkashi district, will also be closed today at 10:28 AM. After the closure, the ceremonial Utsav Doli of Goddess Yamuna will proceed to Kharsali, her winter abode. Devotees will be able to offer prayers and seek blessings at Kharsali for the next six months. It may be noted that portals of Badrinath Dham will be closed for the winter season on November 16. Sakshi Singh, Akashvani News, Dehradun.”

In Uttar Pradesh, Bhai Dooj and Yam Dwitiya is being celebrated with traditional fervour all over state and especially in Mathura Vrindavan.

 

“Thousands of devotees are taking Holy dip in Yamuna river since early morning on the occasion. Devotees from all over the country reach Mathura today particularly brothers and sisters take Holy dip together in Yamuna river and  after that take the blessings of Yamraj the God of death. As per Hindu tradition, sisters who feed their brothers on the auspicious day of Yama Dwitiya would be forever Saubhagyavati and eating at sisters home bestows long life to brothers. This day is also being celebrated as Bhai dooj. Huge Rush is being seen on the gates of prisons across the state where sisters are waiting in queues to meet their brothers on this occasion to apply the tika to their foreheads and pray for their wellbeing and protection. grand fairs are also being organised at jamthara Ghat of Saryu river in Ayodhya and on the banks of Yamuna in Prayagraj on the occasion of yam dwitiya. SUSHIL CHANDRA TIWARI, AIR NEWS, LUCKNOW.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended greetings to people on the occasion of Bhai Dooj. In a social media post, PM Modi said that the festival symbolizes the love, affection and warmth of the special bond between brothers and sisters. He also wished happiness and prosperity to everyone on the occasion.

Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has expressed confidence that India is on track to achieve its export target of one trillion dollars this year. Addressing the curtain-raiser event for the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 in New Delhi, Mr Goyal said, India has already achieved exports worth approximately 480 billion dollars in the first six months of the financial year, accounting for 48 per cent of the annual target.

 

Talking about the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027, the Commerce Minister said, bringing the entire mobility value chain together at one location made the event particularly attractive to international visitors, who could engage with different segments of the industry in a single visit.

The US House of Representatives has rejected a resolution seeking the impeachment of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over his conduct in office and handling of the ongoing war in Iran. The resolution, moved by Republican Congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky and supported by Democrats, was defeated last night after President Donald Trump expressed strong support for the Defence Secretary. Most Republican lawmakers stood by Hegseth.

 

The vote comes amid growing political challenges for the Republican Party following significant losses in the midterm elections. The war in Iran and the resulting rise in fuel prices have emerged as major issues of concern within the party.

 

The rejection of the resolution may, however, provide only temporary relief to Hegseth, as Democrats are expected to gain control of both chambers of Congress in January, potentially renewing efforts to hold the Defence Secretary accountable.

United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said that Iran is facing extraordinary economic pain from the sanctions imposed by America and there is no need to resume major combat operations against Tehran at present. After a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris, Rubio said, US President Donald Trump has concluded that America’s objective is being achieved by economic means and there is no need to resume military action. The US Secretary of State said this will keep growing every day, warning that it will get worse over time. However, Rubio issued a warning for Iran, saying if the country crosses any red lines, the US military stands ready. Rubio blamed Iran for the sanctions, claiming the economic pain has been imposed by the Iranian regime on its own people.

India and France have discussed enhancing cooperation in supply chain resilience, critical technologies, cyber security and industrial partnerships. The discussions were held during the inaugural meeting of the India-France Economic Security and Critical Technologies Dialogue co-chaired by Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and Secretary General Martin Briens of the French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs in Paris yesterday. The External Affairs Ministry said, both sides noted that the dialogue complemented the Innovation Roadmap 2030, India-France Year of Innovation, the existing Economic and Financial Dialogue and the objective of doubling bilateral trade in the next five years. They agreed to work on the priorities identified during the dialogue. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri concluded his two day visit to France yesterday.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Grandmaster. In a post on social media, Mr Modi celebrated the milestone and praised Shrivatri for his achievement, while highlighting the dedication and hard work that have helped Indian players make their mark on the global stage. Mr Modi also pointed to the growing popularity of chess among youngsters, noting that the emergence of players from different parts of the country is particularly encouraging. The Prime Minister said, India reaching 100 Grandmasters is a remarkable milestone that reflects the immense talent, dedication and hard work of our players as well as the growing popularity of chess among our youth. He said, it is particularly heartening to see young chess talents emerging from different parts of the country and making their mark on the global stage. The Prime Minister expressed hope that Shrivatri’s achievement would encourage more youngsters to take up the sport and pursue excellence.

 

Shrivatri, who hails from Madhya Pradesh, secured the Grandmaster title after winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship on Sunday.

In the Under-19 Asia Cup Cricket, India have secured a place in the semi-finals after defeating the United Arab Emirates by 70 runs at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman yesterday. Put into bat first, India posted 309 for 7 in 50 overs riding on an impressive 160 run knock of Aryavir Sehwag. He played 168 balls to score the ton and was adjudged player of the match. Chasing the target of 310 runs the UAE were restricted to 239 in 50 overs. India will now take on Afghanistan in the semi-final tomorrow.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 years. Addressing the jawans on the occasion of Diwali in Bastar, Chhattisgarh yesterday, Prime Minister compared India’s welfare architecture over the past 12 years to a Diwali Rangoli where small, distinct lines come together to form a grand picture.

Prime Minister Modi said, the poor families whose entire lives used to be spent only in worry have now received the assurance of the government, and a new self-confidence has come into them.

The Prime Minister detailed the special development drive in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas that built over 15,000 kilometers of roads, over 9,500 mobile towers, nearly 175 Eklavya schools, around 50 ITIs, 50 Skill Development Centres, and thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs, alongside rehabilitating surrendered Naxals and bringing water, electricity, and roads to remote tribal villages for the first time under PM JANMAN.

Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone for various development projects worth 1,024 crore rupees in Ahmedabad, Gujarat today. A Report:

“Union Minister Amit Shah will dedicate and lay the foundation stone for a total of 30 development projects worth 1,024 crore rupees in his Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency. These projects primarily include various civic amenities by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, such as housing and water supply schemes. His schedule will begin with the inauguration of the four-kilometer-long flyover stretching from ISKCON to Sanand on the SG Highway. Following this, he will inaugurate a newly built Knowledge Hub and dedicate an Urban Health Centre in city. He will also visit the housing scheme units in Vadaj. Concluding his itinerary, Mr. Shah will attend a public event in Ranip, where he will also conduct the draw for the housing scheme beneficiaries. Harshal Pandya Akashvani News, Ahmedabad.”

National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) capped trade margins on MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs, based on the recommendations of Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. The revised prices of these drugs come into effect from today. As on date, 76 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRP for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. Reduction in the MRP have been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50 percent reduction and the highest reduction being 96.45 percent. Further, out of the 137 identified anti-cancer drugs, there are 10-15 drugs which are yet to be launched in India. However, Trade Margin Rationalization (TMR) will be applicable on these drugs also as and when they are launched.  As a result of the price reductions to be effected from today, the estimated annual savings to consumers would be 3,502.31 crore rupees.

He noted that the state, with its picturesque mountain landscapes, sacred rivers and the holy Char Dham, also has a distinct identity rooted in its cultural heritage.

Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen’s Hodeidah and Sana’a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country. The Indian Embassy in Yemen yesterday said, all seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. In a social media post, the Embassy thanked all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of the stranded Indian nationals.

Leaders, scientists, civil society representatives, activists and others from nearly 200 countries, including India, are gathering for two weeks in Turkey’s Mediterranean resort city of Antalya for the 31st Conference of Parties to the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), beginning today, with aim to accelerate clean energy, scale up climate finance and strengthen resilience. The summit will continue till November 20.

The Conference of the Parties (COP), the highest-level global climate summit held annually under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), is bringing together heads of state, Ministers, scientists, business leaders, and civil society representatives from around the world and serves as the primary platform for negotiating and advancing collective action to combat climate change. At COP31, the World Metrological Organisation (WMO) will support countries by providing authoritative scientific observations and information on the state of the global climate system, including through the launch of its flagship State of Climate update 2026, a science-based annual assessment of climate indicators and impacts.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog yesterday formally tasked Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after he secured recommendations from 67 of the 120 elected members of the parliament, compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Eisenkot, a former chief of the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), has 28 days to form a government and secure the approval of the Knesset — Israel’s parliament. He may seek an additional 14-day extension from Herzog for government formation.

The October 27 elections, seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership, produced no clear majority but divided the political landscape into two competing blocs, with the anti-Netanyahu alliance recommending Eisenkot.

National Entrepreneurship Day is being observed today. The day highlights the importance of entrepreneurship in India’s development journey. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was also established on this day in 2014. With over 2.62 lakh Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade-recognised startups, India has emerged as the world’s third largest startup ecosystem, creating employment and expanding opportunities for its youth. A report:

“Over the past decade, youth have increasingly moved beyond the role of beneficiaries to become active contributors to national development. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship has informed that startups have been able to create more than 23 lakh jobs till March this year. The Government has recognized over 55 thousand 200 startups during 2025-26 which is the highest number of startups recognized in a single year since 2016. Along with this, more than 1 lakh recognized startups have at least one woman director or partner. Government initiatives like Startup India, Atal Innovation Mission, Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Startup Hub, Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE) 2.0 Scheme, Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups initiative, National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme and Swavalambini Scheme have supported innovation, easier access to finance, digital platforms, mentorship and enterprise creation. Their expanding contribution reflects India’s growing entrepreneurial capacity and the potential of innovation-led enterprises to support long-term, inclusive development. Saumya Sharan for Akashvani News, Delhi.”

A day after Diwali, a thick blanket of smog engulfed several parts of Delhi this morning, as air quality in the national capital continued to remain in the ‘Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 368 at 7 AM today. According to popular belief, performing puja and making purchases during the auspicious hours on this day brings happiness, wealth, and prosperity to the household. People mostly buying gold, silver, utensils, vehicles, and other new items is a long-standing tradition on Dhanteras.

Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi who played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

In a major overhaul of Agnipath scheme, the Union Cabinet has approved a revised framework creating a pathway for 100 percent absorption of all willing Agniveers into the Defence Forces. Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani said, the move follows an extensive evaluation by the armed forces that gave highly positive feedback on Agniveer efficacy, physical fitness, and technological adaptability.

 

The decision comes just before the first batch of 18,300 Agniveers completes its initial four-year tenure next month.

 

“As originally planned, the top 25% of Agniveers will be offered regular permanent employment immediately after their initial 4-year tenure based on merit. The remaining 75% of Agniveers will now be given an additional engagement period of two years, subject to candidate willingness and recommendations from the forces.

 

Upon finishing the additional two-year extension (bringing total service to 6 years), all remaining willing Agniveers will be offered permanent enrolment as regular soldiers, provided they meet standard selection criteria.

The newly added two-year extension period will feature increased monthly remuneration, an enhanced Seva Nidhi package, and cumulative seniority benefits.

 

The structural reforms effectively remove the mandatory 75% exit provision, ensuring that any Agniveer who wishes to serve permanently and meets the benchmark criteria will have a direct route to do so. YASHASVI KIRYAL, for Akashvani News, DELHI.”

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to provide for immediate suspension of manufacturing licences in respect of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality on specified critical quality parameters. The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance in the interest of patient safety and public health.

 

“The Health Ministry said that under the existing provisions, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. The Ministry added that the proposed amendment also provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension. The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective Root Cause Analysis and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action to the satisfaction of the concerned Licensing Authority. The Ministry said that the amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers. The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation and  objections and suggestions have been invited  from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days. With ANAND KUMAR, SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

The Uttar Pradesh Board of Secondary Education has decided to introduce a new format of answer sheets for the 2027 High School and Intermediate examinations. The move aims to make the examination system more secure, transparent and free from malpractices.

 

“Under the new arrangement, answer sheets will have a single main cover carrying a QR code. On scanning the code, the logo of the Uttar Pradesh Board of Secondary Education will appear. The Board has also decided to use different colours for answer sheets of Class 10 and Class 12. For High School, the A copies will be dark orange and B copies dark blue. For Intermediate, the A copies will be purple and B copies green. The Board has also made special arrangements for the security of answer sheets. They will be kept in secure rooms under round-the-clock CCTV surveillance. Serial numbers of answer sheet bundles will also be recorded in registers to ensure proper monitoring of their storage and distribution. The High School and Intermediate examinations will be held from the 5th to the 24th of February, 2027. Om Awasthi, akashvani news, Lucknow.“

US President Donald Trump acknowledged that the eight-month-old war in Iran heavily impacted the midterm elections. Speaking to reporters at the White House after the midterm election results, Trump conceded that voters were deeply frustrated by the surging gas prices tied to the conflict.

 

“Democrats swept the polls taking control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. US Vice President JD Vance distanced himself from the administration’s military strategy, and said that “the reason we lost is the war”. Meanwhile, Mike Johnson of Louisiana announced he will not seek reelection as House Republican leader, setting up an intense intra-party leadership battle.

 

Following the news of the Democratic sweep, global energy markets responded immediately. Brent crude oil futures plunged over 8% down to under 100 dollars a barrel for the first time in nearly a month.

 

Incoming Democratic congressional leaders have pledged a swift legislative agenda focused on lo  wering the domestic cost of gas, groceries, and healthcare, alongside launching sweeping oversight investigations into the Trump administration’s conduct of the war.
